The TikTok Shop Affiliate Center is the hub inside Seller Center where brands connect with creators to sell their products for a commission. It is where you set commission rates, find and invite creators, run Open and Target Collaborations, and track affiliate sales. It is free, it is the starting point for every TikTok Shop brand, and it is also where the manual workload becomes obvious fast.

What the Affiliate Center does

Four core jobs live here:

  • Set commissions. Choose a rate by product or category that creators earn on each sale they drive.
  • Find creators. Search and filter creators by category, GMV, engagement, and follower range.
  • Run collaborations. Launch Open Collaboration (any eligible creator can promote) or Target Collaboration (you invite specific creators, often with free samples).
  • Track performance. See which creators are driving sales and how much affiliate GMV you are generating.

The Center is where a simple operating loop lives. One seller summarized that loop as "1 to 3 hero products, a strong TikTok-exclusive offer, competitive creator commissions, consistent sample outreach, clear hooks, not rigid scripts" (@jordantwestecom on X). Most of those levers, commissions, collaborations, and creator search, are set right here.

Open vs Target Collaboration

This is the distinction that trips up new sellers.

  • Open Collaboration sets a public commission any eligible creator can pick up without approval. It scales discovery passively but only works when your product, commission, and reviews are attractive enough to get picked up.
  • Target Collaboration lets you invite specific creators directly, usually with a free sample and sometimes a custom commission. It is how you land the creators you actually want.

Most brands run both: Target to recruit proven sellers, Open to catch inbound interest. Full breakdown in Open vs Target Collaboration.

How to use it well

  • Seed through Target Collaboration. Send samples to a curated first wave of 15 to 25 category creators. See creator seeding.
  • Set commission by margin. Not one blanket rate. See commission rates.
  • Filter by selling behavior. Sort for creators who already sell in your category, not the biggest followings. See how to find creators.

Where it breaks down

The Affiliate Center is capable, but it assumes you have the hours. Its limits show up quickly:

  • Coarse search. Filtering is basic, and vetting hundreds of profiles by hand is slow.
  • No real outreach automation. Inviting and following up with creators one by one does not scale past a certain point.
  • Thin management tooling. Reactivating quiet creators, promoting winners, and running briefs all happen outside the Center.

That is why brands graduate to dedicated software or a managed agency once the operation outgrows manual work.

The takeaway

The Affiliate Center is where every TikTok Shop program starts and where you should learn the mechanics. It is free and it works. Just know that its ceiling is your time, and plan for the day the manual load becomes the bottleneck.

Outgrowing manual outreach already? Book a call, or search creators faster than the native tool allows.
